summary.headline: Pennar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3.6% to INR884.55 crore while PBT grew 16% to INR46.8 crore, with PBT margin at 5.38%.
summary.overview: Revenue growth was moderate as legacy steel, railways and diversified businesses shrank, but EBITDA rose 13.3% to INR106.8 crore and PBT rose 16% to INR46.8 crore. Management attributed margin gains to mix shift toward PEB US and engineering services, though PEB India margins dropped for a month or two due to delayed steel pass-through. Order books are at record levels in PEB India (INR1,008 crore), PEB US (above USD100 million) and boilers (INR150.75 crore), while Hydraulics orders softened on US tariff uncertainty. Management guided to double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth in Q2 and reiterated a 7% PBT margin target over about three years. Questions on segment EBITDA, employee cost growth, other income and the promoter warrant issue drew deferred or defensive answers.

segments.name: PEB India
segments.commentary: Order book at record INR1,008 crore; execution hit by engineering clearance and delivery issues, and PEB margins fell over 200 bps for a month or two until steel price increases were passed through. Management expects margins to recover from Q2.

segments.name: PEB US (Ascent)
segments.commentary: Order backlog crossed USD100 million (about USD70 million cited in one answer as the prior-quarter level), revenue running ahead of plan; US revenue stream described as the highest-margin unit with operating margins above 15%.

segments.name: Engineering Services (structural engineering, BIM)
segments.commentary: Structured engineering grew 26.3%; annual revenue about INR70 crore, mainly US and Europe. Management says productivity gains of 30-35% are being used against AI-driven automation risk.

segments.name: Boilers
segments.commentary: Order backlog at record INR150.75 crore; first industrial power boiler achieved as pre-qualification reference, and first pharmaceutical-sector orders won.

segments.name: Hydraulics
segments.commentary: Order backlog about INR30 crore; US activity slowed on tariff uncertainty while Europe performed well. Management is in wait-and-watch mode; the business is about INR100 crore a year.

segments.name: Tech Pennar
segments.commentary: Named as the weak spot: thin order book and execution issues at some customers; a new sales team is in place with improvement expected from Q2.

segments.name: BIW (body-in-white)
segments.commentary: Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026 with three programmes; management expects revenue to double over the next three months on a scheduled order basis.

segments.name: Legacy businesses (steel, railways/Cadnum, tubing)
segments.commentary: About INR1,300 crore annual revenue, now about 25% of group revenue and declining; capital is no longer being deployed and management is seeking a value-realisation structure similar to the solar JV with Zetwerk.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth expected; PEB margins expected to return to prior levels from Q2.
FY27: management says 20% PAT growth is the stated goal for the year; ROCE target about 25-30% for the year (Q2 above 20%).
Debt-to-equity target about 0.7 by year-end FY27; management says anything above 0.7 is unacceptable, with INR20 crore of the promoter's INR50 crore commitment already in.
Over three years PBT margin target of about 7%, from 5.38% now.
Management said it expects the combined entity to grow at double-digit rates from Q2 as higher-growth units scale, while legacy units decline.
capex_capacity: PEB India capacity is available, but execution was hit by engineering clearance delays and labour constraints, which management says are resolved.
PEB US and India advance payments fell to about 25% from 5-10% earlier, as the company moved to reduce working capital.
BIW Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026; three programmes in place.
Management is deliberately building raw-material inventory ahead of expected PEB revenue, which weighed on working capital.
Management is not deploying capital into legacy businesses (steel, railways, Cadnum aerospace); no material capex.
demand_pricing: Record order books across PEB India, PEB US and boilers; the company says the larger backlog is now ready to execute.
Hydraulics bookings below expectations on US tariff uncertainty; Europe performed well.
Steel price pass-through was delayed for about 1-2 months, which compressed PEB margins.
Management says it has about 6-7% share of an addressable market of INR2.25-2.3 lakh crore, and an obtainable market of about INR80,000 crore.
Solar JV with Zetwerk: Pennar holds 45% of a 2 GW capacity entity with potential revenue of about INR4,000 crore; no current revenue numbers were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is expected for full-year FY27 given the 0.8 debt-to-equity target, and is the Q2 level above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management's stated ROCE target is around 30%, but it guided to a full-year average of about 25% and said Q2 would be above 20%. The debt-to-equity target was later framed as 0.7, not 0.8.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PEB India EBIT margin fall more than 200 bps versus peers that passed on steel price hikes, and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel pass-through was delayed for about a month or two, and most of it is now in place. Margins are expected to return to prior levels from Q2, which management called a momentary blip.

qa_highlights.question: How much PEB revenue growth to expect in Q2 at PEB India, PEB US and at company level?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance. Management said PEB overall should see double-digit growth sequentially and year-on-year in Q2, with company-level PEB revenue growth described as high.

qa_highlights.question: Why are employee costs up 16% and will INR400-500 crore be the annual run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs rose on the Telco acquisition, US hiring and engineering/production ramp-up ahead of order backlog. Management accepted that profit must grow faster than salary costs for operating leverage, and gave no annual employee-cost figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a warrant issue to the promoter at INR168, and why not buy shares in the open market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management framed the warrants as a measure of promoter commitment, with INR50 crore committed and INR20 crore already in. It said the price was set through price discovery and governance process, and open-market buying was not ruled out but would be disclosed to exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: Will the segment EBITDA breakdown be disclosed, and what is the other-income outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Segment EBITDA was deferred to next quarter as the data is not yet prepared for disclosure. On other income, management said the components (forex, investment gains, export incentives, write-backs) are recurring in nature and it is priced into operating margin targets.

qa_highlights.question: Why does PBT margin target keep moving, and what caps long-term PAT margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 7% PBT margin over about three years is the guide, and that PAT margin of about 10% is the practical ceiling given 15-20% operating margins and the roughly half-to-PAT conversion. Competitors are at 7-8%, and it called this a Mount Everest target rather than a hard limit.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 delivery: management guided to double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth and PEB margin recovery; a miss would test the credibility of the recovery narrative.
Employee cost growth of 16% YoY (US +37%) against slower revenue growth of 3.6%; watch whether operating leverage shows up in Q2.
Hydraulics order intake under US tariff uncertainty; management is in wait-and-watch mode.
Tech Pennar execution and order book; a new sales team is in place with improvement expected from Q2.
Working capital and interest cost: interest at about 4.18% of revenue is above the internal target and the ~4% long-term guide; debt-to-equity target of about 0.7 by year-end FY27.
Lack of segment EBITDA disclosure (deferred to next quarter), no solar JV revenue numbers, and no diversified-engineering legacy split; governance and disclosure questions remain open.
key_quotes: Revenue growth was moderate this quarter. A few segments moved a little slower than planned, but profitability held up because we have the business quite tightly on cost tactics.
I would strongly suggest you see this as a momentary blip, we are extremely confident that operating margins move back to where they were for PEB India and for PEB U.S. from this quarter onwards.
Other than that, one piece tell you we will be growing and scaling our other revenue streams.
So, we -- as I mentioned, one of our customers, they are a multibillion -dollar firm in the U.S. that spent a lot and try to automate some work.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order books and the growth narrative, but defensive and deferred on disclosure: segment EBITDA, JV revenue, the warrant rationale and the goalpost-moving criticism were met with promises to revert or appeals to commitment rather than numbers.

adds.what: BIW Hyundai body-in-white plant (three programmes), commissioned August 2026

growth.why: Management guides to 20% PAT growth for FY27 and double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth from Q2, backed by record order books in PEB India (INR1,008 crore), PEB US (above USD100 million) and boilers (INR150.75 crore), plus the newly commissioned Hyundai BIW plant expected to double revenue over three months.
